title: Banks race to ramp up AI defenses as deposits fall after cyberattacks
key_facts: Demand deposits at South Korea's five largest lenders (KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori and NH NongHyup) fell from 675.5 trillion won on 30 Sep to 655.4 trillion won on Sunday, a drop of more than 20 trillion won ($15 billion) in 11 days, according to industry officials.
Fixed-term deposits, which had risen five months in a row, fell by more than 2.7 trillion won to slightly over 1 quadrillion won.
On 1 Oct Shinhan Bank reported about 25,000 customers affected, with names, phone numbers, annual income and loan limits exposed; KB Kookmin reported 119 and Hana Bank 89 affected customers.

KB Kookmin plans to raise its information security budget to over 100 billion won next year from 86.1 billion; Woori is considering a rise of more than 20 percent and at least 10 percent more specialist staff; Shinhan promises the industry's highest level.

Banks use AI tools to test their own defences: Woori uses Theori's Xint, KB Kookmin is testing tools with several security firms, NH NongHyup plans an AI red-teaming system in the second half of next year and Hana is building real-time response systems.
ARTEX, the Chinese open-source AI security tool reportedly used in the attacks, is no longer being developed for public release, but copies already downloaded remain in circulation.
quote_evidence: Because security personnel cannot manually keep up with attacks that use AI, we are working to make greater use of AI in our own defenses, an official at a major bank said.
On Oct. 1, Shinhan Bank first reported that about 25,000 customers were affected, with names, phone numbers, annual income and loan limits exposed.
This, however, doesn't affect copies that have already been downloaded and in circulation, meaning the move is unlikely to prevent further attacks using ARTEX.
why_it_matters_hint: The breaches are costing the banks customer deposits and pushing them to spend more on AI-assisted defence.
notes: The article links the deposit fall to the breaches through 'industry officials' but gives no breakdown of other causes.
